To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
attitude, perceived norms, perceived susceptibility, and test site characteristics are the main predictors of STI testing intentions among adolescents attending vocational schools in the Netherland.
the psychosocial determinants of STI testing in adolescents attending vocational schools in the NL are attitude, norms, susceptibility and accessibility.
the psychosocial predictors of STI testing behavior among vocational students were: attitude, perceived norms, perceived susceptibility, and test site characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a group of adolescents at high risk for STIs who have not been targeted before.
the identification of psychosocial correlates that can be used as a foundation for health promotion interventions that encourage STIs testing among adolescents attending vocational schools.
the development of effective interventions that encourage adolescents to participate in STIs testing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has identified the psychosocial factors associated with STI testing intention, and that these factors can be used in the design of interventions aimed at motivating young people to test for STI.
adolescents attending vocational schools are at high risk for STI and that they are less likely to participate in ST testing compared to adolescents attending regular schools.

the present study provides important empirical input for the design and development of health promotion intervention aimed at motivating vocational school students in The Netherlands to participate in sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important factor for STI testing among students attending vocational schools is their attitude toward the testing.
adolescents attending vocational schools are at substantial risk for STI but do not intend to participate in STIs testing.
we have shown the importance of attitudes and norms for adolescents to test for sexually transmitted infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adolescents are willing to test for STIs if they are motivated.
the psychosocial determinants of STI testing are different from those for condom use and sexual risk behavior.
the psychosocial predictors of STI testing in adolescents attending vocational schools are similar to those identified among other adolescent populations.
